meta.titre: International Sports Bodies: what FIFA, the IOC and CAF do and what they mean for Africa
meta.sous_theme: Organisations that run world and African sport, and their link with peace and friendship

sections.contenu_markdown: When the Indomitable Lions of Cameroon reached the quarter-finals of the World Cup in 1990, fans in Yaounde and Douala poured into the streets in joy. Behind every World Cup, Olympic Games and Africa Cup of Nations is an international organisation with rules, officials and a headquarters. In the GCE you may be asked to name those bodies, to say what they do, and to say why sport matters for peace between nations. This course gives you the names and the facts you can be sure of.

items: Sport means organised physical competition governed by rules.
An international organisation is a group set up by many countries or national federations to work together.
Peace means the absence of war and the presence of understanding between peoples.

sections.titre: Who runs world sport: FIFA, the IOC, CAF and the role of sport in friendship
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The main bodies

| Body | Sport / region | Key facts |
|---|---|---|
| FIFA | World football | Founded in 1904 in Paris; headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland; organises the World Cup, held every four years since 1930 |
| IOC (International Olympic Committee) | Olympic Games | Founded in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin; headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland; first modern Games in Athens in 1896 |
| CAF | Football in Africa | Founded in 1957; headquarters in Egypt; organises the Africa Cup of Nations, first played in 1957 |
| World federations | Athletics, basketball, volleyball and others | Each sport has its own world body that sets rules and organises championships |

### What these bodies do

1. They make and update the rules of each sport so that matches are played the same way everywhere.
2. They organise competitions and choose the countries that host them.
3. They run development programmes, for example to train coaches and build facilities in poorer countries.
4. They discipline players, clubs and officials who break the rules, including those who use banned drugs.
5. They promote friendship and fair play between peoples, which is why the Olympic movement speaks of peace.

### Africa and Cameroon

South Africa was the first African country to host the World Cup, in 2010. Cameroon reached the quarter-finals in 1990, won Olympic football gold in 2000, and has won the Africa Cup of Nations several times, including in 2000 and 2002. Apartheid South Africa was kept out of the Olympic Games from the 1960s until 1992, an example of sport being used to protest against injustice.

### Why these bodies matter

They bring people from different countries, languages and religions together under the same rules. They give young people a goal, create jobs and bring tourists, and they give small countries a place on the world stage.

variantes.nom: Naming question (which body, which country, which year)
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for a single name, place or date
variantes.contenu_markdown: Match the sport to its body: football and the World Cup to FIFA, the Olympic Games to the IOC, African football to CAF. For places, remember South Africa as the first African host of the World Cup and Switzerland as home to FIFA and the IOC. Write only the name asked for.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks what these organisations do, or how sport helps peace
variantes.contenu_markdown: Choose three roles (rules, competitions, development) and explain each in a sentence. For peace, give a concrete link: teams from rival countries meet under the same rules and many fans follow the results together. Add a Cameroon example such as 1990 or the Africa Cup of Nations to show you know local history.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how international sports organisations help to promote friendship between nations. [6 marks]

etapes.action: Underline the command word and the key idea.
etapes.justification: 'Explain how' means you must describe a link between the organisations and friendship.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Aim: three developed ways, with examples.

etapes.justification: Three well-explained points earn more marks than six short ones.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. Common rules. 2. Competitions bringing nations together. 3. Fair-play and anti-discrimination rules.

etapes.justification: A reason shows why the way leads to friendship.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Bodies such as FIFA set the same rules for all teams, so every nation plays on equal terms.

etapes.justification: A concrete event proves the point.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The World Cup and the Olympic Games bring athletes and fans from many countries together every four years; the Africa Cup of Nations does the same for African nations.

etapes.justification: The last point links sport to values, and the conclusion ties the answer together.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Rules against discrimination and cheating teach respect, and the exclusion of apartheid South Africa from the Olympics showed sport's support for equality.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: International sports organisations promote friendship between nations in three main ways. First, bodies such as FIFA and the IOC set the same rules for every team, so all nations compete on equal terms and no country is favoured. Second, they organise competitions such as the World Cup, the Olympic Games and the Africa Cup of Nations, which bring athletes and supporters from many countries together and give them a shared experience. Third, they promote fair play and oppose discrimination, which teaches respect between peoples; the exclusion of apartheid South Africa from the Olympic Games until 1992 showed this. In conclusion, by providing common rules, regular meetings and shared values, these organisations help to build understanding between nations.

items.pourquoi_faux: FIFA is the world body for football. The Olympic Games are organised by the International Olympic Committee.
items.correction_markdown: Write that FIFA runs the World Cup, and that the IOC is responsible for the Olympic Games.

items.erreur_markdown: "The first African country to host the Olympic Games or the World Cup was Cameroon."
items.pourquoi_faux: Cameroon has not hosted the World Cup. South Africa was the first African host of the World Cup, in 2010. Cameroon hosted the Africa Cup of Nations in 2022, which is a different competition.
items.correction_markdown: Write 'South Africa' for the World Cup and keep Cameroon for its own achievements, such as the 1990 quarter-final.

items.erreur_markdown: "CAF is the world governing body for football."
items.pourquoi_faux: CAF is the Confederation of African Football, which governs football in Africa. The world governing body is FIFA.
items.correction_markdown: Say that CAF organises football in Africa, while FIFA organises world football.

items.erreur_markdown: In a question on the importance of sports bodies, a student lists only the names of competitions.
items.pourquoi_faux: A list of names does not explain a role or an importance. It earns few marks.
items.correction_markdown: Explain what the body does with each competition, for example 'FIFA sets the rules and organises the World Cup, so all countries play the same game'.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Name the international body that governs world football.
(b) Name the first African country to host the World Cup.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **FIFA** (the International Federation of Association Football).
(b) **South Africa** (2010).

Award one mark for each correct answer.

items.enonce_markdown: Give **two** functions of international sports bodies and explain one of them. [4 marks]
items.solution_markdown:
Function 1: making the rules of the sport. Function 2: organising competitions. Explanation of function 1: common rules mean that a match in Douala is played in the same way as a match in Paris, so teams from different countries can compete fairly. Alternatively explain function 2: competitions such as the World Cup bring nations together every four years.

Award one mark for each function and two marks for a clear explanation. Total: **4 marks**.

items.enonce_markdown: "Sport can bring peace between nations." Discuss, using examples from Africa. [10 marks]
items.solution_markdown:
For: sport brings peoples together under common rules; the Africa Cup of Nations and the World Cup give supporters from different countries a shared event; fair-play rules teach respect; the exclusion of apartheid South Africa from the Olympics until 1992 helped to pressure for equality. Against: sport has also been used to show rivalry between countries, and cannot by itself stop a war; competitions can lead to fights between fans or to boycotts. Judgement: sport can **help to build understanding, but cannot replace political solutions**.

Award marks for knowledge (4), explanation of both sides (4) and a judgement (2).

items_markdown: FIFA governs world football and organises the World Cup; the IOC governs the Olympic Games; CAF governs African football.
South Africa was the first African host of the World Cup, in 2010.
These bodies make rules, organise competitions, support development and discipline offenders.
Sport promotes peace by bringing nations together under common rules and shared values.
In a long answer, give three developed points with an African or Cameroonian example.
